messages:
sam (Acme): Hey team — noticed Reserved GPU hours for our Dedicated pool (org acme-42) dropped ~14% overnight while token usage stayed flat. Dashboard shows 180h remaining at 00:00, invoice shows 152h consumed. Can you help? We didn't change traffic.

maya (support): Sorry to see this, @sam. Can you paste org id, model routes affected, and the window? Also any job/task churn? :eyes:

sam (Acme): Org: acme-42. Affected routes: /v1/generate-prod (pinned to rdx-13b-q4). Window: 2026-03-14 22:00 -> 2026-03-15 06:00 UTC. No deploys from our side. Token counts in our logs are consistent with normal load (~2.1M tokens for the window).

maya (support): Ok thanks. @jordan can you pull metering export for acme-42 for that window? Include GPU_seconds, burst_credits_used, and any reserved->burst toggles.

jordan (billing): pulling now. Initial glance: metering shows a spike in gpu_seconds between 2026-03-15 01:12 and 01:25 — about 18k GPU-seconds. That maps to ~5 GPU-hours. But that doesn't fully explain 28h gap. Digging into autoscaling events.

sre-hannah: I see repeated scale-up/scale-down events around the same timeframe. Runtime created ephemeral worker pods for model warming and then immediately recreated them — looks like failed warmups causing retries. Crashloop+recreate would increment billed GPU time while not showing as token usage. Attaching snippet from runtime logs:

alex (eng-runtime): fyi this pattern matches an existing issue where quantized weight streaming triggers a fallback path that spins extra workers for checksum validation — bug logged as RDX-3891. Those workers are billed as reserved GPU time even though they don't handle requests.

maya (support): Can you paste the exact error/snippet? Also, @sam can you confirm if you had quantization toggles or model refreshes scheduled?

sam (Acme): We don't touch model configs. No scheduled refreshes.

sre-hannah: log snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T01:12:44Z] worker-init id=wx-7f3 init quant-stream
[2026-03-15T01:12:46Z] worker-fatal id=wx-7f3 checksum-mismatch, retrying
[2026-03-15T01:12:48Z] worker-term id=wx-7f3 billed_gpu_seconds=360
````
Multiple retries for different worker ids — each billed.

jordan (billing): Cross-checking metering with invoices: invoices aggregate GPU-hours by reservation bucket but our billing pipeline didn't exclude these transient workers from reserved-hours accounting. That explains the mismatch between dashboard (which subtracts burst credits correctly) and invoice (which used raw metering). Looks like double-counting reservation hours when fallback workers run.

maya (support): Action plan:
- short-term: we can grant provisional SLA credits to Acme for the unexplained portion while we confirm root cause (need sign-off from finance)
- mitigate: temporarily disable quantized streaming fallback for Acme pool to stop spawning extra workers (hotfix)
- long-term: fix RDX-3891 so transient workers are marked as non-billable to reserved accounting and are billed to 'system-maintenance' discriminator.

alex (eng-runtime): Hotfix ready to deploy to staging. Validation steps for repro:
1) Run model warmup with streaming weights: curl -X POST https://runtime.redwood.ai/warmup -H 'x-org: acme-42' -d '{"model":"rdx-13b-q4","stream_weights":true}'
2) Observe worker spawn/retry pattern in runtime logs
3) Check metering export: SELECT sum(gpu_seconds) FROM metering WHERE org='acme-42' AND ts BETWEEN '2026-03-15 01:00' AND '2026-03-15 02:00' AND worker_type='ephemeral';

maya (support): @sam do you want us to apply hotfix to your Dedicated pool now? We can also backdate a provisional credit while we complete the fix.

sam (Acme): Yes please apply hotfix asap. We'll take provisional credit while you resolve root cause.

jordan (billing): Noted. I'll queue provisional credit for 28h pending finance sign-off and link to incident RDX-3891. Will follow up with exact credit amount.

sre-hannah: After hotfix we should monitor for any similar spikes for 72h. I'll add a dashboard alert for ephemeral GPU-second delta > 1h/hr.

deploy-bot: deployment rdx/hotfix/stream-fallback -> staging: success

alex (eng-runtime): Rolling to production now for acme-42 pool. ETA 10m.

deploy-bot: deployment rdx/hotfix/stream-fallback -> prod: success

maya (support): Done — hotfix rolled. @sam monitor dashboard and let us know if the reserved hours stop draining.

sam (Acme): Thanks team. Dashboard shows no further unexpected drains so far. Appreciate the quick turnaround. :thumbsup:

maya (support): We'll keep this thread open until post-72h monitoring completes and finance posts the final credit. Closing notes will be added to the incident tracker.
